facts.text: Two automatic braking systems can reach the same peak deceleration at very different times, potentially changing the collision outcome.
facts.quote: Two systems can produce the same peak deceleration but reach it at very different times; for automatic braking that can change the collision outcome.

facts.text: In the FAA's second worked example, simulated and measured peaks differ by only 0.3%, which would appear excellent under a peak-only metric.
facts.quote: the simulated and measured peaks differ by only 0.3%, which would look excellent under a peak-only metric

facts.text: In the FAA's second worked example, the time-history comparison error is 60.4%, despite simulated and measured peaks differing by only 0.3%.
facts.quote: the simulated and measured peaks differ by only 0.3%, which would look excellent under a peak-only metric, but the time-history comparison error is 60.4%.

facts.text: Validation of the proposed machine's automatic braking should cover the whole causal timing chain rather than only minimum stopping distance: detection time, decision time, brake command time, pressure build-up, deceleration history a(t), speed history v(t), and position history x(t).
facts.quote: validating the whole causal timing chain, not only minimum stopping distance: detection time, decision time, brake command time, pressure build-up, deceleration history a(t), speed history v(t) and position history x(t).

facts.text: Simulation and physical tests for the proposed machine's automatic braking should also compare distance-to-object and relative-speed histories, particularly near the collision or no-collision boundary.
facts.quote: Distance-to-object and relative-speed histories should be compared as well, particularly near the collision or no-collision boundary.
